name: Battle of Hattin

phases.title: The Crusaders camp on the dry plateau
phases.text: The Frankish army could not reach Tiberias by nightfall and turned towards the springs of Kafr Hattin. The Muslims placed themselves between the Franks and the water, so the Franks camped on the arid plateau, closely surrounded.

phases.title: Archers shoot into the smoke-blinded camp
phases.text: Smoke from the fires set by Saladin's forces blinded the Crusaders. Gökböri's mounted archers, resupplied with 400 loads of arrows during the night, shot at the Franks.

phases.title: The army breaks camp and is blocked
phases.text: Amalric formed the battle lines, and the thirsty Crusaders broke camp and changed direction for the springs of Hattin. Saladin's army attacked their ragged approach and blocked the route forward and any retreat.

phases.title: Raymond charges twice towards the lake
phases.text: Count Raymond charged twice to break through to the water at Lake Tiberias. The second charge took him to the lake and he made his way to Tyre.

phases.title: The infantry flee to the Horns of Hattin
phases.text: After Raymond escaped, Guy's position was even more desperate. Most of the Christian infantry fled onto the Horns of Hattin and played no further part in the battle.

phases.title: Guy tries to pitch the tents again
phases.text: Guy attempted to pitch the tents again to block the Muslim cavalry. The knights and mounted serjeants were disorganised but still fought on.

phases.title: The Franks charge Saladin's position
phases.text: The Franks on the hill made a formidable charge on the Muslims facing them and drove them back to Saladin, who was overcome by grief.

phases.title: The Muslims rally and drive the Franks up the hill
phases.text: Saladin rallied his men. The Muslims returned to the fight and climbed the hill, and the Franks withdrew before them.

phases.title: The Franks charge a second time
phases.text: The Franks rallied and charged again as they had the first time, and once more drove the Muslims back to Saladin, who acted as he had on the first occasion.

phases.title: The Muslims drive them back and Guy's tent falls
phases.text: The Muslims turned on the Franks and drove them back to the hill. The Crusaders, surrounded and after three charges, were broken up and defeated, and then Guy's tent fell.

note: The accounts do not give a map of the field. The Springs of Kafr Hattin, the Horns of Hattin and the lake are placed by judgement so that the march runs from left to right towards the water; the positions of the Frankish divisions in the march are not stated beyond the vanguard and rearguard, and the main body is placed between them.
